note: Conflicts between a source published or read during the Edition 1.2 pass and an accepted normalized track. Each row keeps its track failed closed, publishes the source and the conflict, and defers the substantive legal-design correction to a bounded follow-up pass. No memo was silently changed and no normalized track object was edited. Recording a conflict is not resolving it. The authored rows below are passed through unchanged by `npm run rcap:reconcile-master-library`, which recomputes only the totals.

rows.acceptedNormalizedTreatment: The Iowa memo models `ia-9079` as a composed alternative in which the post-July-2013 branch is nothing to file and the pre-2013 branch does contemplate a participant application, held unavailable because it has no form, no rule and thin statutory mechanics. That unit carries the single Iowa build blocker.
rows.conflictingEvidence: Iowa Code § 907.9(4)(b) and 2012 Iowa Acts ch. 1054 (HF 2379) were read in full on 2026-08-03. The self-executing sentence — that the court's criminal record with reference to the deferred judgment shall be expunged upon discharge from probation — already existed in Code 2011 and traces back to 1988 Acts ch. 1168. What HF 2379 added was expungement of dismissed counts and related charges, a statutory definition of "expunged", the state court administrator's secure statewide deferred-judgment docket due 1 July 2013, and mechanics for dismissed-count expungement. No primary Iowa source establishes a distinct pre-2013 participant filing vehicle; secondary commentary asserting an application requirement was not corroborated by any Judicial Branch guidance, form or rule.
rows.requiredResolution: Determine on primary authority whether a pre-July-2013 deferred judgment required any participant filing at all. If it did not, the unit is a no-filing guidance branch rather than an unavailable application branch, and the build blocker resolves by reclassification rather than by acquiring a form.
rows.interimTreatment: The unit stays unavailable and `ia-9079` stays failed closed on the existing build blocker, which is preserved exactly. Edition 1.2 performed no Iowa legal-design redo.

rows.acceptedNormalizedTreatment: The Maine normalization records that CR-308 exists — Order on Motion to Seal Criminal History, Rev. 06/26 — where the retained review recorded no proposed order for any ch. 310-A route, and treats that as closing the proposed-order gap.
rows.conflictingEvidence: The official CR-308 binary was acquired from the Maine Judicial Branch forms portal on 2026-08-03. Its full title is *Order on Motion to Seal Criminal History for Victims of Sex Trafficking or Sexual Exploitation*, and it is a narrow form created under 15 M.R.S. § 2262-B by LD 1871, effective 29 July 2026. It is not a generic proposed order paired with CR-218 and does not serve the general ch. 310-A routes.
rows.controllingAuthority: 15 M.R.S. § 2262-B; Maine PL 2025 (LD 1871); Maine Judicial Branch form CR-308, Rev. 06/26
rows.requiredResolution: Determine whether a general ch. 310-A proposed order exists under another form number, or whether the general routes have no published proposed order and require a custom-drafted one. Then correct the Maine memo's proposed-order components in a bounded legal-design pass.
rows.interimTreatment: CR-308 is published by Edition 1.2 with its true scope recorded. The general ch. 310-A proposed-order components stay unmanifested and the affected tracks stay failed closed. The Maine memo is unchanged.

rows.acceptedNormalizedTreatment: The Indiana normalization carries a component whose official form ID is "CCA-XP-0120-7002 Form ACR", and a separate "Confidential Information Form" component, treating the Coalition for Court Access number and Form ACR as one document.
rows.conflictingEvidence: Both documents were retrieved on 2026-08-03 and are distinct. **CCA-XP-0120-7002** is the Coalition for Court Access *Confidential Information Form*, published inside the Coalition's expungement packets. **Form ACR** is the Indiana Office of Judicial Administration's generic statewide *Notice of Exclusion of Confidential Information from Public Access*, published at `in.gov/courts/files/form-acr.docx`. A separate finding: the component labelled CCA-GF-0120-3016 as a fee-waiver form is the Coalition's *Appearance by Unrepresented Person in Expungement Matter*, filed alongside a separate fee-waiver motion.
rows.controllingAuthority: Indiana Office of Judicial Administration Form ACR; Coalition for Court Access forms CCA-XP-0120-7002 and CCA-GF-0120-3016
rows.requiredResolution: Split the conflated component into its two real document identities and correct the CCA-GF-0120-3016 role label, in a bounded legal-design pass. Do not remap the component ad hoc in this repository.
rows.interimTreatment: Edition 1.2 publishes Form ACR under its own document identity as a supporting-process asset. The conflated component stays unmanifested and the affected tracks stay failed closed. The Indiana memo is unchanged.

rows.acceptedNormalizedTreatment: `mn_prosecutor_agreed` is composed / mixed with four units and `localFormOverride: true`, scoped `county` over Hennepin, Ramsey and Washington.
rows.conflictingEvidence: The joint § 609A.025 prosecutor-agreement portal was launched in 2019 by the Ramsey and Washington County Attorneys and later joined by Hennepin and at least one further county attorney's office outside the normalized scope. Two independent retrievals on 2026-08-03 named that further county differently — one reported Winona, the other Blue Earth — so the additional participant is identified as existing but is **not** conclusively identified, and neither name is asserted here. Minn. Stat. § 609A.025 itself is unchanged since 2014 c 246 s 7, so this is an implementation-coverage difference, not a change in law.
rows.controllingAuthority: Minn. Stat. § 609A.025; Hennepin County Attorney's Office announcement of the joint expungement tool
rows.requiredResolution: Confirm from the portal's own current participant list which county attorneys' offices participate, then decide whether the track's geographic scope should extend to them. Scope is a legal-design decision on the memo, not a source mapping.
rows.interimTreatment: The track's scope stays exactly as normalized. No per-county relief node was created and none is created here.

rows.acceptedNormalizedTreatment: The Minnesota memo resolves Laws 2026, ch. 70, § 5 on the merits and states its effect on Minn. Stat. § 609A.015, subd. 5.
rows.conflictingEvidence: The Revisor's official history line for § 609A.015 records an additional amendment the memo does not carry: **2025 c 3 art 16 s 18**, alongside 2023 c 52 art 7 s 12, 2023 c 70 art 15 s 5, 2024 c 80 art 8 ss 61–63, 2024 c 123 art 4 s 13 and 2026 c 70 s 5. Its substantive effect on the automatic-expungement provisions was not read in this pass.
rows.controllingAuthority: Minn. Stat. § 609A.015, Revisor of Statutes history line, retrieved 2026-08-03
rows.requiredResolution: Read 2025 c 3 art 16 s 18 in full and record whether it changes any participant-facing statement, eligibility rule or waiting period on the Minnesota automatic routes.
rows.interimTreatment: The affected tracks stay failed closed on their existing release blockers. Nothing in the memo was changed and no eligibility rule was altered.

rows.acceptedNormalizedTreatment: The Missouri normalization maps the § 610.140 conviction route to CR360 at SJRC (10-24), an Edition 1.1 packet-form candidate, and records the obsolete OSCA (11-17) revision as never generated.
rows.conflictingEvidence: `courts.mo.gov` returns HTTP 403 with an explicit anti-automation challenge, confirmed independently on 2026-08-03. The only reachable copy of CR360 was a 16th Judicial Circuit mirror stamped **OSCA (11-17)** — the superseded revision the memo already excludes. The same applies to GN10, whose only reachable mirror is stamped OSCA (10-06). Neither was imported: a secondary copy does not override an available official source, and a superseded copy is not evidence about the current one.
rows.controllingAuthority: Missouri Courts expungement forms index; OSCA forms CR360 and GN10
rows.requiredResolution: Obtain the current CR360, CR145, CR375, CR300, CR301, CR143, CR370, CR310, CR311, GN10 and FI-05 binaries from the Office of the State Courts Administrator through a channel that is not blocked, then manifest them in a successor edition.
rows.interimTreatment: No Missouri binary was imported in this pass. FI-05 and CR301 are retained source-gated from the repository corpus on established identity; the four companion orders stay unmanifested. A blocked retrieval is recorded as a blocked retrieval, never as a finding that a form does not exist.

rows.acceptedNormalizedTreatment: The Montana normalization maps the MMRTA units to the Office of the Court Administrator proposed order and certificate of service, and records that both share the single document ID `MT-OCA-MMRTA` at different hashes.
rows.conflictingEvidence: `courts.mt.gov` was network-unreachable on 2026-08-03 and archived replays 404'd, so no official MMRTA binary could be retrieved. The only reachable copy of the MMRTA certificate of service was a county courtesy mirror that marks itself as provided for information purposes only. **It was rejected and not imported.** The Office of the Court Administrator is confirmed as the MMRTA form issuer under Montana Supreme Court order AF 22-0129, and the Montana Department of Justice CRISS unit is confirmed as the CRISS form issuer.
rows.controllingAuthority: Montana Supreme Court order AF 22-0129; Montana Office of the Court Administrator MMRTA forms page; Montana DOJ / DCI CRISS
rows.requiredResolution: Acquire the official MMRTA Form A, Form B, proposed order and certificate of service from the Office of the Court Administrator, republish the proposed order and the certificate of service under distinct document IDs, and re-class the CRISS form so it can back an official-form component.
rows.interimTreatment: The four hash conflicts and five role mismatches are preserved exactly and appear in the source-acquisition queue. No unofficial substitute was published.
